# Merged-roadmap work on the prerequisite chains of the 100 Annals definitions

Specified in a merged roadmap (`TauCetiRoadmap/<Name>/` at roadmap commit 746ffb289, 2026-11-27), not
yet (fully) implemented in Tau Ceti main (d395922ff82, 2026-11-27), and on the prerequisite chain of at
least one definition. Each item was checked against the README section, STATUS.md (snapshot date
given per roadmap; several are stale) and a grep of Tau Ceti code. Item format: status
(NOT-STARTED / PARTIAL with what exists), ready now (yes / no: needs X), definitions served,
evidence. Section and layer ids are the roadmap's own.

## Key ordering facts across items

- SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.14 (Hilbert/Quot) is the choke point for the Jacobian cluster
  (defs 19, 24, 30, 71, 80, 84, 85). Required order: JacobianChallenge §C.1 coherence (finiteness over a
  Noetherian ring is in code for projective schemes and the relative projective case is ready; the proper case then follows by Chow's lemma over an affine base, which
  is in code) and §C.2 base change, then SSF §4.14, then §D.3 Hilbert quotients and §D.4 projective
  Picard representability, then §D.5 `Pic⁰` and the Abel maps and §D.8 the Jacobian. §D.2
  (`HasPicardScheme`, `picardScheme`) is in code. `Symᵈ X` (§C.4) needs only §C.2, not §4.14; §D.5
  needs it.
- SSF Layer 1 is a linear chain: §1.3 (done), then §1.5, §1.6, §1.7/§1.8, §1.9, then §1.19, §1.20,
  §1.21, §1.22, §1.23. §1.5 is partial (`EtaleEquivRel` with `restrict` and `ofAtlas` and the quotient sheaf
  `quotientSheaf` in code); §1.6 is partial (`spacePresentation` in code, `etaleQuotientTheorem` ready), and §1.8 is ready. §1.18 has `StackInGroupoids`,
  `ofSheaf`/`ofScheme`, `yonedaEquiv`, the generic 2-fibre product, products and the terminal stack (`Stack.pi`, `Stack.terminal`) and the stackification of a prestack as a stack, functorial in
  strong transformations, with `stackificationDiscreteEquiv` for separated presheaves, in code; the universality of stackification is ready now. §1.19 is partial:
  `IsRepresentableBySpaces` is in code, `IsAlgebraicStack` and `IsDeligneMumford` are not.
- LieGroups Layer 7 (compact real form, Cartan involution θ) unblocks Layer 9 beyond `GL n`. Layer 9
  in turn heads the real-reductive chain: ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.F.1 and ALS.0.1–ALS.0.3,
  then AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups §2.3a and §§2.3–2.4, then RealSemisimpleLieGroups Layers 2–5
  and §5.7, for defs 1, 4, 7, 15, 31, 54, 62, 79. Layer 7 is partial (`serreCompactInvolution`, the
  conjugate-linear Chevalley involution of a Serre presentation, and compact real forms with their
  existence, `exists_isCompactConjugation`, and θ = στ|𝔤₀ for a compact form commuting with σ,
  `isCartanInvolution_restrictRealForm`, are in code; conjugating a compact form into a commuting one is not) and ready now. The Cartan-involution
  predicates are in code at the Lie-algebra level (`LieEquiv.IsCartanInvolution`, with the Cartan
  decomposition) and for real affine groups (`TauCeti.IsCartanInvolution`, ALS.0.1); existence and
  conjugacy of Cartan involutions are not.
- EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.0.1 (étale module sheaves) precedes every étale cohomology item
  (§F.1, §F.2.x, §F.4.x). It is partial (geometric stalks, finite lisse sheaves and the monoidal
  structure with monoidal stalks in code), and its constructible part is ready now.
- RiemannianGeometry R5a (B, S, normal connection) is formally blocked on SmoothBundlesConnections
  B3–B4 per its README, though that dependency looks soft: the normal bundle `ν_f` with its
  projection, the derivative along a map `CovariantDerivative.alongMap` and the intrinsic B, S and
  ∇⊥ with the Gauss and Weingarten decompositions, metric compatibility along a map, the Weingarten
  equation, self-adjointness of S and metric compatibility of ∇⊥ are in code. It heads the
  chain R5a, then R5a.2 (on R5a.1's relative volume, which is in code), then R5b (whose operator part,
  `IsCoercive.formOperator`, is in code), then R5c, then MinimalSurfaces MS6, for defs 49, 52, 65,
  66. Varifolds §5.1 and RiemannianManifoldsWithConvexBoundary §3.6 also consume R5a.
- The boundary tangent space, the outward and inward unit normals and boundary defining functions
  (RiemannianManifoldsWithConvexBoundary §§1.1–1.2 and §1.3 except the comparison of defining
  functions; `outwardUnitNormal`, `inwardUnitNormal`, `IsBoundaryDefiningFunctionOn`) and §1.4's pointwise
  `II` (`boundarySecondFundamentalForm`) with its defining-function and normal-extension descriptions are in code, so the rest of §1.3, the rest of §1.4 and
  RiemannianGeometry R7.9 are ready (defs 49, 52, 66). DifferentialGeometry 12.4 (the Riemannian
  density) is ready: 5.5a's `TauCeti.integralDensity` with `integralTopForm_eq_integralDensity` is in
  code; 12.5's unoriented divergence theorem with Green's identities is in code.
- SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.19–1.20 (`IsAlgebraicStack`, points of a stack) head all of
  StackPointsAndResidualGerbes (defs 16, 17, 28, 29), none of whose items can start before them;
  they sit at the end of the SSF Layer 1 chain above.
- VirtualFundamentalClass (defs 16, 27) starts at Layer 0 (stack dimension), which needs SSF Layer 1
  through §1.19 (DM stacks) and §1.21 (quotient stacks); its Layer 1 also needs SSF §§1.10, 1.22 and
  §5.5 (partial: the normal cone of an immersion is in code), and its Layer 3 the cotangent-complex
  chain DerivedModuleAlgebra §0.4, then DerivedDeRhamCohomology §5.8. No item can start now.
- AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry §1.3 `coherentGrassmannian` (partial: the glued relative
  Grassmannian `Scheme.Modules.grassmannian` over any base is in code; its universal quotient and
  universal property are ready) blocks NashBlowups §0.4 and §§1.2–1.5, hence Layers 2, 6 and 7
  (defs 25, 26). NashBlowups §§0.1–0.3 are in code apart from the §§0.1–0.2 Checks; §0.5 is in code apart
  from its cusp Check, and §1.1 is in code; that Check and the rest of §0.6 and of §0.7 can start now.
- LieGroups Layer 9 (`CartanInvolution`, `IwasawaData` beyond `GL n`) also blocks LieGroupsPartII
  Layers 1–3 and §§7.1, 8.1 (defs 1, 4, 54, 79).
- The modular-curve cluster (defs 69, 71, 77) runs through ModularCurvesPartII, whose items wait on
  ModularCurves Layer 10 (untouched), JacobianChallengePartII Layers 0–1 (on JacobianChallenge
  Layers D–E) and EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§F.1–F.4. Only ModularCurvesPartII §3.8 (partial) can
  start now. CompletedCohomologyPartII and CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility §§1.1–1.2
  (def 77) wait on the same ModularCurvesPartII §§14.1–14.4a and on ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces
  §§0.1–0.7.
- ShimuraVarieties §§P.1–P.5 (Hodge structures as representations of the Deligne torus) head both
  Mumford–Tate specifications, ShimuraVarieties §P.3a and ShimuraData Layer 1 (defs 13, 23, 89).
  The direction from Hodge structures to Deligne-torus actions on points, the Hodge decomposition of
  a real `S`-comodule (`hodgeComponent`) and the Mumford–Tate Hopf ideal of an algebraic `h`
  (`mumfordTateHopfIdeal`) are in code, and so is §P.3's round trip from a Hodge structure to its
  representation of `S` and back, the step that makes the construction apply to #13.
- BallQuotientsAndComplexHyperbolicLattices (defs 15, 31) starts from RealSemisimpleLieGroups §5.7,
  hence from LieGroups Layer 9, and its quotients need ComplexComparisonPartII §C-1.1.
- ModularCharactersAndBlocks §0.2 (block idempotents) is in code and so is §6.1 (relative traces,
  the Brauer homomorphism and its kernel, with its Checks); with §1.3 (partial, ready) they head the chain to blocks, defect groups and heights
  (defs 2, 3, 9), and ModularCharactersAndBlocksPartII Layer 6 builds heights on them. Its Layers 1–5
  (Glauberman correspondence, def 8) need only Mathlib and Tau Ceti character theory at the start.
- The CM chain (defs 70, 74, 75) starts from ShimuraVarieties §5.1 `CMType` (partial: CM types, reflex fields, products and primitive pairs are in code; the reflex norm is ready), then
  ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity §1.2 (whose algebraic splitting part is in code),
  then AutomorphicPadicLFunctionsPartII §§0.1, 0.2 and 5.1; the abelian-scheme parts also need
  AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli Layers A1–A5.
- QuasiregularMaps (defs 41, 42) starts with §1.1 (`LinearMap.minimalStretch` and its Checks in code) and §1.2 (the outer and inner distortions, in code) and §1.3 (the comparison of the linear distortions, in code); its §§2.1–2.3
  also need SobolevMapsBetweenManifolds §§4.2–4.3, §5.1 and §§6.2–6.3 (def 47).
- The Néron–Tate height (def 80) is HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions §0.19 (§§0.1–0.8 are in code as
  `TauCeti.HeightClass`, and §0.18's Tate limit as `TauCeti.tateLimit`), which needs AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A1.4–A1.5.
- ReductiveGroups §§9B.5–9B.8 (def 11) define the classical group schemes, which can start now on
  `TauCeti.ConstantForm` and the Clifford API; their comparisons with pinned models wait on
  Layer 9's uniform pinned construction and §§9B.1–9B.3, and the Dickson invariant and smoothness
  on LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles §§2.1–2.2 and DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra §3.3.
- The entropy chain (defs 96, 97) runs from GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic §4.2
  (`measureEntropy`, on ProbabilisticAndMetricNumberTheory §5.1a's finite-label entropy) and
  ArithmeticDynamics §§2.6–2.7 to ClassicalErgodicTheory Layer 4, §§6.1–6.2, Layer 7 and §§8.1–8.2.
  In code are the countable partition entropy, the conditional partition entropy and Kolmogorov–Sinai
  entropy `measureEntropy`, the finite-label entropy `labelEntropy`, the conditional entropy of a finite partition given a sub-σ-algebra,
  finite partitions with small atoms and null boundaries, subadditivity and the Fekete limit
  (GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic §4.2), ClassicalErgodicTheory §0.1's factor maps (also for
  actions, with the invariant σ-algebra) and §5.1's invariant probabilities with their extreme points;
  much of ClassicalErgodicTheory §§4.0–4.1 is in code (conditional entropy given the σ-algebra of a
  countable label, entropy of factors and of isomorphic systems, `measureEntropy_iterate`,
  `measureEntropy_symm`), and Layer 4 from §4.0 on is ready now. Topological pressure (ClassicalErgodicTheory §§5.2, 5.4–5.5) starts
  from Mathlib's `Dynamics.coverEntropy`; `topologicalPressure` and §5.2's metric forms, iterates,
  inverses and Lipschitz bound are in code, and the rest of §§5.2 and 5.4 is ready now.

### §1.5 étale equivalence relations and the quotient sheaf

### Layer 5 (solvable groups) Structure of smooth connected solvable groups, G = G_u ⋊ T
- Status: PARTIAL. Exists: `torus_coinvariants_unipotentRadical` (G/G_u is a torus), and the triviality of homomorphisms from diagonalizable groups to unipotent groups, scheme-theoretically, so a diagonalizable closed subgroup of a unipotent group is trivial (`TauCeti.geometricallyUnipotentPointsCommHopfAlgProperty.bialgHom_eq_unit_comp_counit_of_groupLikeSetSpan_eq_top`, Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Unipotent/Diagonalizable.lean, on `Module.Basis.map_coefficientMatrix_eq_one_of_isUpperTriangular_of_groupLikeSetSpan_eq_top`, Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/UpperUnitriangular.lean); separable base change and descent of the unipotent radical; a diagonalizable closed subgroup or torus meets `R_u(G)` trivially and maps with trivial kernel to `G ⧸ R_u(G)` (`sup_unipotentRadicalDefiningIdeal_eq_augmentation_of_torus`, `kernelHopfIdeal_coinvariantsι_unipotentRadical_comp_mkQuotient_eq_augmentation_of_torus`, Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Unipotent/Radical/Diagonalizable/Basic.lean). Split extensions of affine groups are semidirect products: if a closed subgroup `T` maps isomorphically onto `G ⧸ R_u(G)` then `R_u(G) ⋊ T → G` is an isomorphism (`TauCeti.CommHopfAlgCat.isIso_productMapOfNormal_of_isIso`, HopfIdeal/Normal/Product/Split.lean; `FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.isIso_productMapOfNormal_unipotentRadical_of_isIso`, Unipotent/Radical/SemidirectProduct.lean), which reduces `G = G_u ⋊ T` to the isomorphism of a maximal torus onto `G ⧸ G_u`. A homomorphism of finite-type affine groups with geometrically reduced source and trivial kernel is a closed immersion, and an isomorphism of smooth connected groups when it does not drop the Lie dimension (Milne 5.34), `TauCeti.CommHopfAlgCat.surjective_iff_kernelHopfIdeal_eq_augmentation_of_isGeometricallyReduced`, `isIso_of_kernelHopfIdeal_eq_augmentation_of_finrank_le` (Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/ClosedImmersion.lean), applied to a closed subgroup `T` meeting a normal subgroup such as `R_u(G)` trivially, `TauCeti.FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.isIso_coinvariantsι_comp_mkQuotient` (HopfIdeal/Coinvariants/ClosedImmersion.lean); for a maximal torus this leaves the dimension count `dim T ≥ dim G/G_u`. Over a perfect field (Milne 16.33(a)–(c)), `G ⧸ R_u(G)` is a torus (`FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.torus_coinvariants_unipotentRadical_of_perfectField`, Solvable/UnipotentRadical/Basic.lean) and the unipotent radical commutes with every field extension (`FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.baseChangeHopfIdeal_unipotentRadicalDefiningIdeal_of_perfectField`, Solvable/UnipotentRadical/PerfectField.lean, with `unipotentRadicalDefiningIdeal_eq_of_multiplicativeType_coinvariants`, Unipotent/Radical/Torus/Quotient.lean). Over an algebraically closed field, a torus `T` of a connected reduced `G` with `dim Lie(G ⧸ R_u(G)) ≤ dim Lie(T)` maps isomorphically onto `G ⧸ R_u(G)` and `R_u(G) ⋊ T → G` is an isomorphism: `FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.isIso_coinvariantsι_unipotentRadical_comp_mkQuotient_of_torus`, `isIso_productMapOfNormal_unipotentRadical_of_torus` (Unipotent/Radical/Torus/Complement.lean). Missing: the existence of a torus of dimension `dim(G/G_u)` in a connected solvable group (so that `G = G_u ⋊ T` holds for maximal tori), and conjugacy of subgroups of multiplicative type into T by G_u(k̄) (Milne, Theorem 16.33(b),(d)). STATUS lists Layer 5 as done. Layer 5's comodule definition of unipotence is in code: `TauCeti.unipotentCommHopfAlgProperty` with `unipotentCommHopfAlgProperty_iff`, `hasNonzeroFixedVector`, `exists_basis_coefficientMatrix_isUpperUnitriangular`, `unipotentCommHopfAlgProperty_iff_forall_exists_basis`, the agreement with the geometric-point definition over an algebraically closed field `unipotentCommHopfAlgProperty_iff_geometricallyUnipotentPoints` (Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Unipotent/Comodule.lean) and the unipotence Checks (Examples/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Unipotent/Comodule.lean), including that `SL_n` is not unipotent, `TauCeti.Examples.UnipotentSpecialLinear.not_unipotent_specialLinear` (Examples/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Unipotent/SpecialLinear.lean). Quotients of unipotent groups are unipotent, `unipotentCommHopfAlgProperty.of_injective`, and homomorphisms from a unipotent group to a diagonalizable group are trivial, `unipotentCommHopfAlgProperty.apply_eq_algebraMap_counit_of_groupLikeSetSpan_eq_top` (Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Unipotent/Morphism.lean). Invariance of unipotence under extension of the base field (Milne, Corollary 14.9), `unipotentCommHopfAlgProperty.baseChange_iff`, is in open Tau Ceti PR https://git.taucetiproject.org/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/pulls/6910 (Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Unipotent/FieldExtension.lean). The Layer 5 Check that the Frobenius kernel `αₚ` is unipotent over every field of characteristic `p` is in code: `TauCeti.AlphaP.unipotentCommHopfAlgProperty_coordinateRing` (Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/AdditiveFrobeniusKernel/Unipotent.lean), through the power basis of its coordinate ring and the injective truncation coalgebra map `AlphaP.truncationCoalgHom_injective` (AdditiveFrobeniusKernel/PowerBasis.lean, Unipotent.lean), with unipotence inherited along injective coalgebra maps `unipotentCommHopfAlgProperty.of_coalgHom_injective` (Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Unipotent/Morphism.lean).
- Ready now: yes. It is the input that Layer 7 torus conjugacy, and through it the root datum, wait on.

For an ordinary algebra `A` and an `A`-bimodule `M`, the Hochschild coboundary `TauCeti.hochschildBimoduleCoboundary` (RingTheory/HochschildCohomology/Coboundary.lean) and the cochain complex and cohomology with bimodule coefficients, `TauCeti.hochschildBimoduleCochainComplex`, `hochschildBimoduleCohomology` (RingTheory/HochschildCohomology/Bimodule.lean, Tau Ceti PR #37750); matrix Morita invariance of `HHⁿ`, `TauCeti.hochschildCohomology.matrixExtensionEquiv` (HochschildCohomology/Matrix.lean).
